text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Tuesday.

LONDON - Stocks fell on concern about weakness on Wall Street and the prospect of a six-week domestic election campaign, dealers said. The blue-chip FTSE 100 index lost 16.5 points to 4,356.8, after bouncing off a low of 4,340.1.

FRANKFURT - Worries about a possible delay for Europe's single currency and the fate of U.S. interest rates pushed German shares down to a two-week low in a choppy session. The DAX lost 59.80 points to 3,291.19 points, dropping below the 3,300-point level for the first time since early March.

PARIS - French shares fell for the second consecutive session on doubts about the timetable for a single European currency, a weaker dollar and volatile U.S. markets ahead of the Federal Reserve's meeting on March 25. The CAC-40 index lost 14.43 points to 2,573.95.
ZURICH - Swiss shares fell, with the broad Swiss Performance Index off 20.38 points to 2,871.46.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks jumped, as market participants rejoiced over the government's decision to draw up plans to boost the stagnant land market by the end of the month. The 225-share Nikkei average gained 391.70 points to 18,445.20.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks slumped, dragged down by fears of higher interest rates and profit-taking. The Hang Seng Index fell 89.62 points to 12,748.91, shedding most of Monday's 102 point gain.
SYDNEY - Australian shares closed lower in line with a rapidly fading futures market. The All Ordinaries index lost 23.1 points to 2,404.3.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended a lethargic day weak. The overall index fell 26.9 points to 7,085.5, the industrial index shed 10.9 points to 8,321.6 and the gold index lost 20.4 points to 1,370.3.
